communication-01.meaning: “Pesan” means a message or communication conveyed to someone. It also has other senses, including advice, an instruction, or an order.
communication-01.common_use: Common and readily understood for written and digital messages; it is also used in phrases such as “pesan suara” (voice message).
communication-01.preferred: A natural, broadly usable choice for “message.” For app-based texting, “chat” is also common, especially when referring to the conversation or chat feature.
communication-01.register: Neutral; the word itself is not informal, though its exact sense depends on context.
communication-01.region: Standard contemporary Indonesian; no specific regional limitation identified.
alternatives: chat (especially for app-based messaging or a chat conversation)

claims.proposition: KBBI-derived entry defines pesan as an instruction, advice, request, or message conveyed through another person; contemporary digital usage also applies it to messages sent in apps.
Indonesian-language sources use pesan for WhatsApp messages and distinguish it from chat as a conversation or app feature.
Pesan is a neutral general term for a message, while chat is a common alternative when the context is app-based conversation.

source_leads.exact_claim: The entry gives senses including a request, advice, instruction, or message conveyed through another person; this is a third-party KBBI mirror, not the official dictionary site.
The article uses pesan in its description of WhatsApp group messages.

communication-03.meaning: “Obrolan” means light, informal conversation. It can refer to an online chat, though its dictionary sense is not specifically limited to digital communication.
communication-03.common_use: Common and understood for casual conversation; “chat” is also frequent in app and messaging contexts.
communication-03.preferred: “Obrolan” is a natural Indonesian choice for an informal conversation. For the app feature or act of texting online, speakers may use “chat” or “ngobrol.”
communication-03.register: Neutral to informal; the word commonly describes relaxed conversation.
communication-03.region: Standard contemporary Indonesian; no specific regional limitation identified.

claims.proposition: A KBBI-derived entry defines obrolan as light, relaxed conversation or empty talk.
Indonesian-language sources use obrolan as a label for online chat or as an Indonesian gloss for chat.
Obrolan fits informal conversation broadly; chat is a common alternative when referring specifically to digital messaging or an app feature.

source_leads.exact_claim: The page gives the KBBI-derived definition “percakapan ringan dan santai; omong kosong”; this is a third-party dictionary mirror.
The document labels a Microsoft Teams feature “Obrolan (chat)” and describes it as a private conversation.
An Indonesian government app manual uses “Semua Obrolan” as the title for a chat list.

communication-05.meaning: “Balas” means to answer or respond; “membalas” is the usual active verb form meaning to reply, including to a letter or message.
communication-05.common_use: Common and readily understood. In casual digital contexts, people also say “balas chat” or “balas pesan.”
communication-05.preferred: For “to reply,” “membalas” is a clear standard form. In casual conversation, “balas” is also widely used, often in constructions such as “balas chat.”
communication-05.register: “Membalas” is standard and neutral. Bare “balas” is common in informal speech and messaging.
communication-05.region: Standard contemporary Indonesian; no specific regional limitation identified.
alternatives: menjawab (answer; often a question or call)

claims.proposition: The KBBI-derived entry defines membalas in part as answering a letter or similar communication.
Indonesian-language sources use balas and membalas for replying to WhatsApp messages or chat.
Membalas is a standard neutral verb for replying; balas is a common informal form, especially in digital chat phrases.

source_leads.exact_claim: The entry for membalas includes “menjawab (surat dan sebagainya)” (answering a letter and similar communication); this is a third-party KBBI mirror.
The article uses “balas pesan” in its title and instructions for replying to WhatsApp group messages.
The police IT directorate article uses “membalas chat” for replying to WhatsApp Web chats.

communication-06.meaning: “Pesan suara” means a voice or audio message sent to someone. It can refer to a digitally recorded message, distinct from a live call.
communication-06.common_use: Established and readily understood, including in WhatsApp-related reporting and instructional material. “Voice note” and “VN” are also used in contemporary conversation.
communication-06.preferred: “Pesan suara” is a clear Indonesian term and works well in neutral contexts. In informal messaging, “voice note” or “VN” may be more familiar to some users.
communication-06.register: Neutral Indonesian; “voice note” and “VN” are informal borrowed expressions.
communication-06.region: Used in contemporary Indonesian; no specific regional limitation identified.
alternatives: catatan suara (less established as the everyday term)

claims.proposition: Indonesian-language sources define pesan suara or voice note as a short recorded audio message sent through a messaging app or social platform.
Indonesian news and public information sources use pesan suara alongside voice note for the WhatsApp audio-message feature.
Pesan suara is a clear neutral Indonesian equivalent; voice note and VN are common informal alternatives, but available sources do not establish which is more frequently preferred in everyday speech.

source_leads.exact_claim: Defines voice note as a short recorded audio message sent through messaging apps or social media and gives pesan suara as an Indonesian translation.
Calls WhatsApp voice note a pesan suara feature.
An Indonesian government app manual uses the heading “Kirim Pesan Suara (Voice Note).”

communication-07.meaning: “Panggilan video” means a call with live video. It distinguishes a video call from a voice-only call.
communication-07.common_use: Common and readily understood. Indonesian news sources use panggilan video and video call, sometimes together.
communication-07.preferred: “Panggilan video” is a clear neutral Indonesian expression. “Video call” is also common in contemporary everyday usage, especially in technology contexts.
communication-07.register: Neutral; video call is an English loan phrase used informally and in media coverage.
communication-07.region: Standard contemporary Indonesian; no specific regional limitation identified.

claims.proposition: Indonesian-language sources use panggilan video for a call that lets participants communicate through video.
Indonesian news coverage uses both panggilan video and video call for the same communication feature.
Panggilan video is a natural Indonesian wording; video call is also common, and available sources do not establish a single everyday preference across speakers.

source_leads.exact_claim: ANTARA describes the WhatsApp feature as “panggilan video” in its Indonesian-language report.
The article refers to “panggilan video atau video call” as equivalent terms.
The article uses “panggilan video (video call)” in an Indonesian-language guide.
